takeaways: Splash 1.4.0 has the lowest T_turn in every band

k2 (Swift 1.5 IQ4_XS GGUF on Splash) takes 6.6 s at 256K and 6.7 s at 512K, against 9.2 and 12.7 s for w1, the same fine-tune in MLX on mlx-serve 26.10.3 (the daily driver). The gain comes from decode, ~106 tok/s up to 512K against 57–74; the cold prefill is the same (731 and 732 tok/s at 256K). The comparison mixes runtime and weight format: Splash loads Flash-Next from a GGUF only.
Only Splash reaches 1M

k2 serves 1,000,000 tokens with KV int8 and the KV past ~860K tokens on its SSD cache: 9.3 s per turn, decode ~77 tok/s, 16.9 GB of headroom. A cold 1M prompt takes 25.5 min. mlx-serve 26.10.3 loads 1M (YaRN 3.815 + KV 4-bit) and serves the cold prompt in 28.6 min, but the next requests fail with PrefillDoesNotFit (~18 GB needed, 7–9 GB free): 2 of 5 for w1, 3 of 5 for n3.
On one mlx-serve build, Swift 1.5 beats the iQ pack past 128K

On mlx-serve 26.10.3 with the same flags, n3 (iQ-MLX 4.7 bpw) and w1 (Swift 1.5) tie up to 128K (8.0 and 8.9 s). At 256K n3 takes 11.9 s against 9.2 s, and at 512K 14.5 s against 12.7 s. On 26.10.1 the iQ pack took 9.8 and 13.0 s: the iQ pack lost speed on 26.10.3, Swift gained.
Splash re-prefills a changed history

middle_mutation reuses nothing on Splash in every band (hit 0), against ~0.45 on mlx-serve. Splash keeps the hybrid recurrent state only where a request ends, so an edit, a compaction or a branch before that point re-prefills the whole prompt: 25 min at 1M (incoai/splash #387, #361).
k2 keeps its quality to 1M

At 262144, k2 passes the quality floor against w1 in all six suites. Against k2 at 262144, it passes all six at 512K and five at 1M: HumanEval at 1M sits one question under the margin, within run noise. The long-context probe answers 8/8 at 256K, 512K and 1M. Tool calls: 20/20 sessions with frequency_penalty 0.
GSQ-RCO-Coder: fastest on Splash, weak on GPQA

g2 (IQ1_M GGUF on an unofficial Splash build from main 3135ab4) has the lowest T_turn of the campaign, 6.3 s at 256K; its quality was not measured. g1 (the MLX pack on mlx-serve 26.10.3) fails the GPQA floor: 31/50 against 43/50 for w1.
mlx-serve 26.10.1 leads the four runtimes of the engine round
n2 has the lowest T_turn of n2, o1, m1 and d1 from 8K to 512K: 7.8, 8.2, 8.8, 9.8 and 13.0 s, with the tool turn under 3 s up to 256K and 3.9 s at 512K (KV 4-bit).
oMLX is second at 128K and 256K
o1 T_turn is 12.1 s at 128K and 14.5 s at 256K. MTPLX is second at 8K and 32K (8.2 and 8.8 s). oMLX has no YaRN, so it stops at 262K.
MTPLX fits 128K only with --memory-limit max

The vendor default plans a 65,536-token window on this 128 GB M4 Max and refuses 128K. With --memory-limit max MTPLX serves 128K in 15.1 s (3 reps), but the cold prefill runs at 274 tok/s against 759 on n2. It refuses 256K: the memory-plan fit is 237,568 tokens. KV q8 is ignored for Flash-Next, and the sparse QSA prefill fails to allocate without the M5 NAX kernels.
ds4 serves 512K, slowly
d1 serves every band up to 512K (YaRN 2.0), but decode stays at 43–54 tok/s and the warm tool turn grows from 6.4 s at 128K to 50 s at 512K. T_turn: 16.4 s at 128K, 61.9 s at 512K.
Quality: o1 and MTPLX within ±1–5 cases of n2

HumanEval 164 at temperature 0, with the prompt imports added: n2 156, o1 157, MTPLX (m1x) 151 (10 answers truncated in reasoning). The strict bench2 grade (154 / 140 / 132) fails answers without from typing import. Tool calls: jdhodges 38 / 36 / 35 of 40, Veerman 9 / 10 / 10 of 12. The n2 run (2026-10-07) used about 200 tokens per answer against 1,800 (o1) and 3,300 (m1x), so the reasoning mode was likely not the same: read this as a sanity check, not a ranking.

gates_glossary.desc: hit ≥ 0.90 on append and tool_turn at 32K and 128K.
needles at 10/50/90 correct at 32K and 128K; a truncated answer (reasoning > 4096 tokens) does not count as a failure.
swap delta ≤ 0.5 GB in every band.
zero HTTP 4xx/5xx errors or stream errors at 32K and 128K.
a peak above 102 GB raises a warning and does not eliminate: it is the normal operating point of mlx-serve.

stage_u.note: u1 is the abliterated pack on the same runtime and quant as c1 (identical config.json). The legitimate refusal probe scores 40 prompts in four categories that aligned models often over-refuse, plus 10 neutral controls; there a refusal is a defect and it stores 200 characters per answer. The harmful probe scores 24 prompts a safe model must refuse (offensive cyber plus drug, weapons, fraud, and violence anchors); there a refusal is the safe answer and it stores only the verdict, never any response text.

quality.note: Temperature 0, max_tokens 32,768, one run per arm. HumanEval 164: the strict grade is bench2.py as-is; it runs only the code in the answer, so an answer without from typing import fails. "With imports" adds the import lines of the prompt before the answer (regrade_humaneval.py). n1 and n2 ran on 2026-10-07 and answered with about 200 tokens per question; o1 used about 1,800 and m1x about 3,300, so the reasoning mode was likely not the same. Read the table as a sanity check, not a ranking. Truncated = the answer spent the 32,768 tokens in reasoning and wrote no code.
